pairs.reason: Implementation 1 converts to Celsius before checking absolute zero, so tiny sub-zero source values (e.g. -1e-14 K) get absorbed by rounding and pass, while Implementation 2 checks exactly in the source unit. Implementation 2's tests also cover boundaries across all target units and more invalid-unit inputs.

Both check absolute zero exactly in the source unit, and Implementation 2 adds a same-unit shortcut, but it adds no tests at all and relies on an implicit fall-through to Kelvin in its if-chains. Implementation 1's data-driven linear-scale table is compact and comes with a relevant test suite.

Both validate exactly in the source unit; Implementation 2's six pairwise formulas repeat the magic constants and expose a public ABSOLUTE_ZERO, while Implementation 1 pivots through Celsius using a named constant. Implementation 2's tests are somewhat broader, but Implementation 1's structure will be easier to maintain.
